# Shader chunks

<!-- Generated by packages/xtree/scripts/shader-docs.mjs from packages/xtree/src/shaders. Do not edit; run `pnpm shaders:docs`. -->

xtree ships its GLSL building blocks as chunks: plain GLSL ES 3.00 strings that you include by id. `resolveIncludes` expands each chunk once, even if several shaders or chunks include it, and adds `#line` directives so compile errors name the chunk.

```ts
import { resolveIncludes, formatShaderError } from '@mk7s/xtree/glsl';
import { noise } from '@mk7s/xtree/shaders/noise';

const { code, files } = resolveIncludes(
  `#include <xtree/noise/simplex>
  void main() { gl_FragColor = vec4(vec3(xt_simplex(vUv * 8.0) * 0.5 + 0.5), 1.0); }`,
  noise,
  { name: 'my-effect.glsl' },
);
// Pass `code` to a ShaderMaterial. On a compile error:
// console.error(formatShaderError(gl.getShaderInfoLog(shader), files));
```

Conventions: every name starts with `xt_` (functions and globals) or `XT_` (macros). Chunks never declare `#version` or `precision`, so the host shader decides those; the functions assume `highp`. Hues are in turns, [0, 1). Includes that are not xtree chunks, such as three.js’s `<common>`, are left for three.js to resolve.

## Noise

Import from `@mk7s/xtree/shaders/noise` as `noise`, or every family at once as `chunks` from `@mk7s/xtree/shaders`.

### hash

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/hash>
```

Integer hashes for noise and randomness. Every float result is in [0, 1). Uses the PCG family from Jarzynski and Olano, "Hash Functions for GPU Rendering", JCGT 9(3), 2020.

| Function                                                                                                                         | Description                                                                        |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `uint xt_pcg(uint v)`                                                                                                            | One round of the 32-bit PCG hash.                                                  |
| `uvec3 xt_pcg3d(uvec3 v)`                                                                                                        | Three-dimensional PCG hash (pcg3d).                                                |
| `uvec4 xt_pcg4d(uvec4 v)`                                                                                                        | Four-dimensional PCG hash (pcg4d).                                                 |
| `float xt_uintToUnit(uint v)`<br>`vec2 xt_uintToUnit(uvec2 v)`<br>`vec3 xt_uintToUnit(uvec3 v)`<br>`vec4 xt_uintToUnit(uvec4 v)` | Maps the top 24 bits of a hash to a float in [0, 1).                               |
| `float xt_hash1(float p)`<br>`float xt_hash1(vec2 p)`<br>`float xt_hash1(vec3 p)`<br>`float xt_hash1(vec4 p)`                    | Hashes the bit pattern of a float, vec2, vec3 or vec4 to one value in [0, 1).      |
| `vec2 xt_hash2(vec2 p)`<br>`vec2 xt_hash2(vec3 p)`<br>`vec2 xt_hash2(vec4 p)`                                                    | Hashes a vec2, vec3 or vec4 to two values in [0, 1).                               |
| `vec3 xt_hash3(vec2 p)`<br>`vec3 xt_hash3(vec3 p)`<br>`vec3 xt_hash3(vec4 p)`                                                    | Hashes a vec2, vec3 or vec4 to three values in [0, 1).                             |
| `vec4 xt_hash4(vec4 p)`                                                                                                          | Hashes a vec4 to four values in [0, 1).                                            |
| `vec3 xt_latticeHash(ivec3 c)`                                                                                                   | Hashes an integer lattice point to three values in [0, 1). Used by lattice noises. |
| `vec4 xt_latticeHash(ivec4 c)`                                                                                                   | Hashes a four-dimensional integer lattice point to four values in [0, 1).          |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Jarzynski and Olano, Hash Functions for GPU Rendering, JCGT 9(3), 2020.

### gradient

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/gradient>
```

Uniformly distributed unit gradients for integer lattice points, shared by the gradient and simplex noises.

Includes `xtree/noise/hash`.

| Function                     | Description                                                                  |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vec2 xt_gradient2(ivec2 c)` | Unit gradient for a 2D lattice point.                                        |
| `vec3 xt_gradient3(ivec3 c)` | Unit gradient for a 3D lattice point.                                        |
| `vec4 xt_gradient4(ivec4 c)` | Unit gradient for a 4D lattice point (Shoemake's uniform 3-sphere sampling). |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Shoemake, Uniform random rotations, Graphics Gems III, 1992.

### value

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/value>
```

Value noise: smoothly interpolated random values on an integer lattice. Output is in [0, 1]. Uses quintic interpolation, so the first and second derivatives are continuous.

Includes `xtree/noise/hash`.

| Function                                               | Description                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vec2 xt_quintic(vec2 t)`<br>`vec3 xt_quintic(vec3 t)` | Quintic smoothstep used by lattice noises: 6t^5 - 15t^4 + 10t^3. |
| `float xt_valueNoise(vec2 p)`                          | 2D value noise in [0, 1].                                        |
| `float xt_valueNoise(vec3 p)`                          | 3D value noise in [0, 1].                                        |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Perlin, Improving Noise, SIGGRAPH 2002 (quintic interpolant).

### perlin

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/perlin>
```

Classic gradient (Perlin) noise with hashed unit gradients and quintic interpolation (Perlin, "Improving Noise", SIGGRAPH 2002). Output is in [-1, 1] and is zero at every integer lattice point.

Includes `xtree/noise/gradient`, `xtree/noise/value`.

| Function                  | Description                   |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `float xt_perlin(vec2 p)` | 2D gradient noise in [-1, 1]. |
| `float xt_perlin(vec3 p)` | 3D gradient noise in [-1, 1]. |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Perlin, Improving Noise, SIGGRAPH 2002.

### simplex

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/simplex>
```

Simplex noise in 2, 3 and 4 dimensions (Perlin 2001; corner ordering as described by Gustavson, "Simplex noise demystified", 2005). Gradients are hashed unit vectors and the kernel radius squared is 0.5, so the noise is continuous. Output is in [-1, 1]; the scale factors come from the analytic bound of each kernel sum.

Includes `xtree/noise/gradient`.

| Function                   | Description                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `float xt_simplex(vec2 p)` | 2D simplex noise in [-1, 1].                                                       |
| `float xt_simplex(vec3 p)` | 3D simplex noise in [-1, 1].                                                       |
| `float xt_simplex(vec4 p)` | 4D simplex noise in [-1, 1]. Use the fourth axis for looping or evolving 3D noise. |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Perlin, Noise hardware, SIGGRAPH 2001 course notes; Gustavson, Simplex noise demystified, 2005.

### worley

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/worley>
```

Worley (cellular) noise (Worley, "A Cellular Texture Basis Function", SIGGRAPH 1996). Returns the Euclidean distances to the nearest (F1) and second-nearest (F2) feature points. Uses the standard 3x3 (3x3x3) cell search: F1 is exact for jitter up to 1, and F2 can be slightly too large at full jitter.

Includes `xtree/noise/hash`.

| Function                               | Description                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `vec2 xt_worley(vec2 p, float jitter)` | 2D cellular noise. Returns vec2(F1, F2). `jitter` in [0, 1] moves feature points off the cell centers. |
| `vec2 xt_worley(vec3 p, float jitter)` | 3D cellular noise. Returns vec2(F1, F2).                                                               |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Worley, A Cellular Texture Basis Function, SIGGRAPH 1996.

### fbm

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/fbm>
```

Fractal Brownian motion: octaves of simplex noise, each scaled by `lacunarity` in frequency and `gain` in amplitude. The result is divided by the total amplitude, so it stays in [-1, 1]. Each octave is offset to avoid artifacts aligned at the origin.

Includes `xtree/noise/simplex`.

| Function                                                          | Description                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `float xt_fbm(vec2 p, int octaves, float lacunarity, float gain)` | 2D fBm of simplex noise in [-1, 1]. Typical values: octaves 5, lacunarity 2.0, gain 0.5. |
| `float xt_fbm(vec3 p, int octaves, float lacunarity, float gain)` | 3D fBm of simplex noise in [-1, 1].                                                      |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Musgrave, Texturing and Modeling: A Procedural Approach, 1994.

### curl

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/curl>
```

Curl noise: divergence-free flow fields built from simplex potentials (Bridson, Hourihan and Nordenstam, "Curl-Noise for Procedural Fluid Flow", SIGGRAPH 2007). Derivatives use central differences.

Includes `xtree/noise/simplex`.

| Function                        | Description                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vec2 xt_curl(vec2 p)`          | 2D curl noise: the rotated gradient of a scalar simplex potential.          |
| `vec3 xt_curlPotential(vec3 p)` | Three decorrelated simplex values used as a vector potential.               |
| `vec3 xt_curl(vec3 p)`          | 3D curl noise: the curl of a vector potential made of three simplex fields. |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Bridson, Hourihan and Nordenstam, Curl-Noise for Procedural Fluid Flow, SIGGRAPH 2007.

### blue

```glsl
#include <xtree/noise/blue>
```

Cheap per-pixel dither noise. Interleaved gradient noise needs no texture (Jimenez, "Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare", SIGGRAPH 2014). Blue-noise sampling reads a tiling texture and moves it each frame along the R2 low-discrepancy sequence, so successive frames are decorrelated.

| Function                                                   | Description                                                                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `float xt_ign(vec2 pixel)`                                 | Interleaved gradient noise in [0, 1) for a pixel coordinate (for example gl_FragCoord.xy). |
| `float xt_ign(vec2 pixel, int frame)`                      | Interleaved gradient noise that changes every frame and repeats every 64 frames.           |
| `vec2 xt_r2(int frame)`                                    | Offset of the R2 sequence for a frame, in [0, 1)^2.                                        |
| `vec4 xt_blueNoise(sampler2D tex, ivec2 pixel, int frame)` | Fetches a tiling blue-noise texture at a non-negative pixel, offset each frame along R2.   |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Jimenez, Next Generation Post Processing in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, SIGGRAPH 2014; Roberts, The Unreasonable Effectiveness of Quasirandom Sequences, 2018 (R2 sequence).

## Color

Import from `@mk7s/xtree/shaders/color` as `color`, or every family at once as `chunks` from `@mk7s/xtree/shaders`.

### luminance

```glsl
#include <xtree/color/luminance>
```

Luminance and luma weights.

| Function                             | Description                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `float xt_luminance(vec3 linearRgb)` | Relative luminance of linear Rec.709 / sRGB primaries (ITU-R BT.709).            |
| `float xt_luma601(vec3 encodedRgb)`  | Luma of gamma-encoded RGB with Rec.601 weights, as used by analog video effects. |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: ITU-R BT.709; ITU-R BT.601.

### space

```glsl
#include <xtree/color/space>
```

Color space conversions. Hues are in turns, [0, 1). "Linear" means linear-light sRGB (Rec.709 primaries, D65). HSV, HSL, YIQ and YUV work on whatever RGB encoding they are given; most image effects pass gamma-encoded sRGB.

| Function                        | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vec3 xt_srgbToLinear(vec3 c)`  | sRGB transfer function, encoded to linear (IEC 61966-2-1). Negative values pass through the linear segment. |
| `vec3 xt_linearToSrgb(vec3 c)`  | sRGB transfer function, linear to encoded (IEC 61966-2-1).                                                  |
| `vec3 xt_rgbToHsv(vec3 c)`      | RGB to HSV. Returns (hue in turns, saturation, value).                                                      |
| `vec3 xt_hsvToRgb(vec3 c)`      | HSV to RGB. Hue is in turns.                                                                                |
| `vec3 xt_rgbToHsl(vec3 c)`      | RGB to HSL. Returns (hue in turns, saturation, lightness).                                                  |
| `vec3 xt_hslToRgb(vec3 c)`      | HSL to RGB. Hue is in turns.                                                                                |
| `vec3 xt_linearToOklab(vec3 c)` | Linear sRGB to OKLab (Ottosson, 2020). Returns (L, a, b).                                                   |
| `vec3 xt_oklabToLinear(vec3 c)` | OKLab to linear sRGB (Ottosson, 2020).                                                                      |
| `vec3 xt_oklabToOklch(vec3 c)`  | OKLab to OKLCH. Returns (L, chroma, hue in turns). Hue is 0 for achromatic colors.                          |
| `vec3 xt_oklchToOklab(vec3 c)`  | OKLCH to OKLab. Hue is in turns.                                                                            |
| `vec3 xt_linearToOklch(vec3 c)` | Linear sRGB to OKLCH.                                                                                       |
| `vec3 xt_oklchToLinear(vec3 c)` | OKLCH to linear sRGB.                                                                                       |
| `vec3 xt_rgbToYiq(vec3 c)`      | RGB to YIQ (FCC NTSC). Y in [0, 1], I in about [-0.596, 0.596], Q in about [-0.523, 0.523].                 |
| `vec3 xt_yiqToRgb(vec3 c)`      | YIQ to RGB, the exact inverse of xt_rgbToYiq.                                                               |
| `vec3 xt_rgbToYuv(vec3 c)`      | RGB to YUV with BT.709 weights. U and V are in [-0.5, 0.5].                                                 |
| `vec3 xt_yuvToRgb(vec3 c)`      | YUV (BT.709) to RGB.                                                                                        |

**Credits:** Derived from OKLab (MIT); see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. References: IEC 61966-2-1 (sRGB); Ottosson, A perceptual color space for image processing, 2020; FCC NTSC YIQ; ITU-R BT.709 YUV.

### white-balance

```glsl
#include <xtree/color/white-balance>
```

White balance by von Kries adaptation to D65 in Bradford cone space. The temperature sets the illuminant the scene is assumed to be lit by, as in photo editors: lower values make the image cooler, higher values warmer. The Planckian locus is shifted slightly so that 6500 K with zero tint is exactly D65, which makes the default settings an identity.

| Function                                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vec2 xt_planckianXy(float kelvin)`                              | CIE 1931 xy chromaticity on the Planckian locus, 1667–25000 K (Kim et al., 2002 cubic fit).                                                                                 |
| `vec2 xt_whitePointXy(float kelvin, float tint)`                 | White point for a temperature and a tint in [-1, 1]: the locus shifted to pass through D65 at 6500 K. Tint moves the point perpendicular to the locus; positive is greener. |
| `vec3 xt_xyToBradford(vec2 xy)`                                  | Bradford cone response of a chromaticity at luminance 1.                                                                                                                    |
| `vec3 xt_whiteBalance(vec3 linearRgb, float kelvin, float tint)` | White-balances linear sRGB. Positive tint makes the image more magenta, as in common photo editors.                                                                         |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: Kim et al., Design of advanced color temperature control system for HDTV applications, 2002; Lam, Metamerism and Colour Constancy, 1985 (Bradford transform).

### tonemap

```glsl
#include <xtree/color/tonemap>
```

Tone mapping operators matching three.js r186 (`tonemapping_pars_fragment`), with exposure as an argument instead of a uniform. Inputs and outputs are linear sRGB. Ported from three.js (MIT). AgX follows Filament (Apache-2.0) and the minimal AgX contrast curve published by iolite; Neutral is the Khronos PBR Neutral operator.

| Function                                              | Description                                                                               |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vec3 xt_tonemapLinear(vec3 color, float exposure)`   | Exposure-only tone mapping, clamped to [0, 1].                                            |
| `vec3 xt_tonemapReinhard(vec3 color, float exposure)` | Simple Reinhard: c / (1 + c).                                                             |
| `vec3 xt_tonemapCineon(vec3 color, float exposure)`   | Optimized Cineon filmic operator (Hejl and Burgess-Dawson).                               |
| `vec3 xt_acesRrtOdtFit(vec3 v)`                       | ACES RRT + ODT curve fit (Stephen Hill).                                                  |
| `vec3 xt_tonemapAces(vec3 color, float exposure)`     | ACES filmic, including three.js's 1/0.6 exposure scale for brighter viewing environments. |
| `vec3 xt_agxContrast(vec3 x)`                         | Minimal AgX default contrast curve (sixth-order polynomial fit).                          |
| `vec3 xt_tonemapAgx(vec3 color, float exposure)`      | AgX with Rec.2020 working primaries.                                                      |
| `vec3 xt_tonemapNeutral(vec3 color, float exposure)`  | Khronos PBR Neutral: keeps base colors accurate and compresses only highlights.           |

**Credits:** Ported from three.js (MIT); see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md. References: three.js r186 tonemapping_pars_fragment; Hill, ACES fit (BakingLab); Filament AgX (Apache-2.0); Wrensch, Minimal AgX implementation (iolite); Khronos PBR Neutral tone mapper.

## Blend

Import from `@mk7s/xtree/shaders/blend` as `blend`, or every family at once as `chunks` from `@mk7s/xtree/shaders`.

### modes

```glsl
#include <xtree/blend/modes>
```

Photoshop-style blend modes. Separable and non-separable formulas follow W3C Compositing and Blending Level 1 where it defines them. `base` is the backdrop and `blend` is the source. Modes defined only for [0, 1] (the dodges, burns, light modes, hard mix and divide) clamp their result to [0, 1]. Normal, multiply, add, lighten, darken, difference and the non-separable modes pass HDR values through.

| Function                                                        | Description                                                                                 |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vec3 xt_blendDarken(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                    | Darken: the smaller of each channel.                                                        |
| `vec3 xt_blendMultiply(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                  | Multiply.                                                                                   |
| `vec3 xt_blendColorBurn(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                 | Color burn (W3C).                                                                           |
| `vec3 xt_blendLinearBurn(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                | Linear burn: base + blend - 1, clamped.                                                     |
| `vec3 xt_blendLighten(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                   | Lighten: the larger of each channel.                                                        |
| `vec3 xt_blendScreen(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                    | Screen.                                                                                     |
| `vec3 xt_blendColorDodge(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                | Color dodge (W3C).                                                                          |
| `vec3 xt_blendAdd(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                       | Add (linear dodge). Not clamped, so it is safe for HDR glow.                                |
| `vec3 xt_blendHardLight(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                 | Hard light (W3C).                                                                           |
| `vec3 xt_blendOverlay(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                   | Overlay: hard light with base and blend swapped (W3C).                                      |
| `vec3 xt_blendSoftLight(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                 | Soft light (W3C formula).                                                                   |
| `vec3 xt_blendVividLight(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                | Vivid light: color burn below 0.5, color dodge above.                                       |
| `vec3 xt_blendLinearLight(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`               | Linear light: base + 2 * blend - 1, clamped.                                                |
| `vec3 xt_blendPinLight(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                  | Pin light: darken below 0.5, lighten above.                                                 |
| `vec3 xt_blendHardMix(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                   | Hard mix: 1 where base + blend >= 1, otherwise 0.                                           |
| `vec3 xt_blendDifference(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                | Difference.                                                                                 |
| `vec3 xt_blendExclusion(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                 | Exclusion.                                                                                  |
| `vec3 xt_blendSubtract(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                  | Subtract: base - blend, floored at 0.                                                       |
| `vec3 xt_blendDivide(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                    | Divide: base / blend, clamped. A zero blend gives white wherever the base is above zero.    |
| `float xt_blendLum(vec3 c)`                                     | Luminosity used by the non-separable modes (W3C Lum).                                       |
| `vec3 xt_blendClipColor(vec3 c)`                                | W3C ClipColor: brings a color back into gamut while keeping its luminosity.                 |
| `vec3 xt_blendSetLum(vec3 c, float l)`                          | W3C SetLum: gives `c` the luminosity `l`.                                                   |
| `float xt_blendSat(vec3 c)`                                     | W3C Sat: max channel minus min channel.                                                     |
| `vec3 xt_blendSetSat(vec3 c, float s)`                          | W3C SetSat: gives `c` the saturation `s` while preserving channel order.                    |
| `vec3 xt_blendHue(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                       | Hue: hue of the blend with the saturation and luminosity of the base.                       |
| `vec3 xt_blendSaturation(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                | Saturation: saturation of the blend with the hue and luminosity of the base.                |
| `vec3 xt_blendColor(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                     | Color: hue and saturation of the blend with the luminosity of the base.                     |
| `vec3 xt_blendLuminosity(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                | Luminosity: luminosity of the blend with the hue and saturation of the base.                |
| `vec3 xt_blendDarkerColor(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`               | Darker color: whichever whole color has the lower luminosity.                               |
| `vec3 xt_blendLighterColor(vec3 base, vec3 blend)`              | Lighter color: whichever whole color has the higher luminosity.                             |
| `vec3 xt_blend(int mode, vec3 base, vec3 blend)`                | Blends with a runtime mode (one of the XT_BLEND_* constants). Unknown modes return `blend`. |
| `vec3 xt_blend(int mode, vec3 base, vec3 blend, float opacity)` | Blends with a runtime mode, then mixes the result over `base` by `opacity`.                 |

| Constant                 | Value |
| ------------------------ | ----- |
| `XT_BLEND_NORMAL`        | `0`   |
| `XT_BLEND_DARKEN`        | `1`   |
| `XT_BLEND_MULTIPLY`      | `2`   |
| `XT_BLEND_COLOR_BURN`    | `3`   |
| `XT_BLEND_LINEAR_BURN`   | `4`   |
| `XT_BLEND_DARKER_COLOR`  | `5`   |
| `XT_BLEND_LIGHTEN`       | `6`   |
| `XT_BLEND_SCREEN`        | `7`   |
| `XT_BLEND_COLOR_DODGE`   | `8`   |
| `XT_BLEND_ADD`           | `9`   |
| `XT_BLEND_LIGHTER_COLOR` | `10`  |
| `XT_BLEND_OVERLAY`       | `11`  |
| `XT_BLEND_SOFT_LIGHT`    | `12`  |
| `XT_BLEND_HARD_LIGHT`    | `13`  |
| `XT_BLEND_VIVID_LIGHT`   | `14`  |
| `XT_BLEND_LINEAR_LIGHT`  | `15`  |
| `XT_BLEND_PIN_LIGHT`     | `16`  |
| `XT_BLEND_HARD_MIX`      | `17`  |
| `XT_BLEND_DIFFERENCE`    | `18`  |
| `XT_BLEND_EXCLUSION`     | `19`  |
| `XT_BLEND_SUBTRACT`      | `20`  |
| `XT_BLEND_DIVIDE`        | `21`  |
| `XT_BLEND_HUE`           | `22`  |
| `XT_BLEND_SATURATION`    | `23`  |
| `XT_BLEND_COLOR`         | `24`  |
| `XT_BLEND_LUMINOSITY`    | `25`  |

**Credits:** Original implementation (MIT). References: W3C Compositing and Blending Level 1.
